prompt:
Find real, documented measurements of WLED or ESP32-based LED controller reliability (uptime, failure rates) in long-running installations. Cite the sources and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, here are the documented measurements and observations regarding the reliability of ESP-based LED controllers (specifically ESP8266 and ESP32 running WLED or custom firmware).

### ESP8266 Reliability (Custom Firmware)
A long-term experiment using an ESP8266 module with custom logging firmware demonstrated high stability over several years.

SOURCE: https://www.electrobob.com/led-logger-v3/ | QUOTE: "As of June 2016 I have ended the experiment, once all the strips went over 10.000 hours." | CLAIM: The experimental setup ran continuously for over 10,000 hours until voluntarily terminated.

SOURCE: https://www.electrobob.com/led-logger-v3/ | QUOTE: "The third version of the Led logger has run without any major issues. Based on uptime logging there has never been any freeze or malfunction." | CLAIM: The ESP8266 controller experienced zero freezes or malfunctions during the multi-year experiment.

SOURCE: https://www.electrobob.com/led-logger-v3/ | QUOTE: "And of course, the uptime was measured. Very impressing, as at some point it has reached 4500 hours." | CLAIM: A specific continuous uptime milestone of 4,500 hours was recorded without power loss or reboot.

SOURCE: https://www.electrobob.com/led-logger-v3/ | QUOTE: "This also proves that the ESP8266 module I used as a WiFi connection which is one of the first to hit the market, can function for a long time." | CLAIM: Early-market ESP8266 modules are capable of long-term stable operation in this context.

### ESP32-C3/S2 Reliability (WLED Firmware)
Recent reports indicate significant stability issues with ESP32-C3 and ESP32-S2 devices running WLED, particularly when integrated with Home Assistant or using specific software versions. Failures often manifest as unresponsiveness after a few days.

SOURCE: https://github.com/Aircoookie/WLED/issues/4347 | QUOTE: "After a couple of days, the device because unresponsible within Home Assistant as well as pinging it / access to the WebUI." | CLAIM: ESP32-C3 devices running WLED may become completely unresponsive after approximately 2-5 days of operation.

SOURCE: https://github.com/Aircoookie/WLED/issues/4347 | QUOTE: "I have to remove power to get it working again, and then it will work again for the next 3-5 days." | CLAIM: The failure mode requires a hard power cycle to resolve, with recurrence every few days.

SOURCE: https://github.com/Aircoookie/WLED/issues/4347 | QUOTE: "After downgrading to 0.15.1 on this ESP32-S2 the light currently shows an uptime of 7.5 days with no changes to the hardware, HA setup or power supply." | CLAIM: Downgrading WLED firmware from version 0.15.3 to 0.15.1 resolved stability issues on an ESP32-S2, achieving at least 7.5 days of uptime.

SOURCE: https://github.com/Aircoookie/WLED/issues/4347 | QUOTE: "The current state of knowledge are that there are two reasons for crashes: 1. bad hardware / power design... 2. a bug in async webserver which can be triggered by using HA's aggressive polling system" | CLAIM: Identified causes for ESP32 WLED crashes include poor power design and software bugs in the asynchronous web server when subjected to high concurrency polling.

SOURCE: https://github.com/wled/WLED/issues/5596 | QUOTE: "Receivers oscillate between 10-25 fps achieved with periodic complete HTTP unresponsiveness." | CLAIM: In WLED v0.15.4, ESP32 receivers using DDP virtual-bus fan-out experienced periodic total HTTP unresponsiveness.

SOURCE: https://github.com/wled/WLED/issues/5596 | QUOTE: "after upgrading to v16 it is working again." | CLAIM: Upgrading to WLED v16 resolved the HTTP starvation and unresponsiveness issues on ESP32 receivers.

### Environmental and Hardware Failure Observations
Anecdotal evidence highlights the impact of environmental factors (weather) and component quality on longevity.

SOURCE: https://igor.moomers.org/posts/wled-christmas-lights | QUOTE: "My initial outdoor controller died after the first rain, losing my hard-programmed schedules and presets." | CLAIM: An unprotected ESP32 controller failed immediately upon exposure to rain.

SOURCE: https://igor.moomers.org/posts/wled-christmas-lights | QUOTE: "This version lasted through one wet season, but then shorted out soon after I moved to Berkeley." | CLAIM: A partially protected (hot-glued) ESP32 controller survived one wet season but eventually failed due to moisture ingress.

SOURCE: https://tynick.com/blog/12-17-2019/christmas-lights-with-wled/ | QUOTE: "Previously the roofline LEDs were run using a cheap wifi controller. It had a really bad interface and wasn’t reliable at all." | CLAIM: Generic cheap WiFi controllers were observed to be unreliable compared to ESP-based WLED setups.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Statistical failure rates (e.g., percentage of units failing per year) for large-scale deployments of WLED controllers.
